newsitem.title: INDIA: India's National bourse revises stock price limits.
newsitem.headline: India's National bourse revises stock price limits.

text.p: India's National Stock Exchange (NSE) on Monday relaxed stock price limits in its most active shares to 10 percent from 7.0 percent, traders said.
The NSE said the limits had been relaxed after consulting market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India.
Earlier in the day, a leading NSE official told Reuters the exchange would not relax its daily stock limits.
"The whole purpose of circuit-breakers gets defeated if you relax them the moment they get triggered," the official said.
"We are standing by the position that the whole point of circuit breakers is to allow news to break more gradually," he said.
NSE officials were not immediately available for comment.
Brokers had been expected to relax the daily price limit of seven percent for leading stocks after a political crisis hit Indian share prices on Monday.
Sales in most blue chips were frozen after the shares hit their seven percent limit in early trade.
Price movement of shares at the exchange are subject to certain intra-day and weekly price limits to prevent any sharp volatility in the market, traders said.
